newsitem.title: USA: Saxton hails McDonough support of inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Saxton hails McDonough support of inflation target.

text.p: Joint Economic Committee Chairman Jim Saxton on Friday welcomed New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough's call for inflation-targeted monetary policy.
"I strongly agree with Mr McDonough's support for inflation targeting," a major agenda item at the JEC, Saxton told Reuters.
The New Jersey Republican congressman, who has introduced a bill to focus Fed monetary policy solely on price stability, also said he was working on specific inflation targets.
"I am currently considering other legislative vehicles that may more precisely designate inflation targets as the preferred implementation of the price stability objective," Saxton added.
McDonough in Toronto on Friday said he would prefer that any official inflation target would take the form of a range, not a decimal point, and that Congress should set that target.

"Many of the countries around the world have decided that if you're going to believe in price stability, there should be an inflation target, in which case if we ever had one, I would prefer that it be a range and not a point," McDonough said.

"There is, I think, a very definite question in the United States as to whether (a) that's a good idea, and (b) if so, who should establish it? I have a very strong view that that is the function of the Congress," he added.
McDonough has in the past proposed a target range of 0.5-2.0 percent growth in the core consumer price index as an official Fed benchmark and other Fed officials have made similar comments.

Legislators, including Sen. Connie Mack, R-Fla., have drafted bills in the past to set price stability as the Fed's main goal, which McDonough said would not interfere with sustained economic growth, the Fed's other current mandate.
"Price stability is how you achieve sustained economic growth, so there is no real conflict," McDonough said.
